technique: Cite every finding: a changed file and a RIGHT-side line that appears in the diff, plus the quoted hunk. No citation, no finding.
Report only what you are at least 80/100 confident is a real defect. Smells are labelled 'possible' and carry a fix.
Skip anything a linter or formatter already enforces. No style nits unless the repo's own rules require it.
Classify the change as a one-way or two-way door; read one-way doors (migrations, public API removal, auth, deploy config) hardest.
If there is no spec or issue, say so; never invent requirements.
Large diffs: focus on the highest-impact files and say coverage was limited.

items.check: Does the diff do what the PR title/body says, fully, without scope creep?
Objective bugs in changed code: null/undefined paths, races, off-by-one, wrong conditions, stale state.
Unhandled promise rejections, swallowed errors, async without error handling, uninformative errors.
String-built SQL, unsafe HTML rendering of input, shell commands built from input.
New endpoints/IPC without auth checks; inconsistent permission checks; session handling.
Hardcoded secrets, tokens or PII in code, logs or error messages.
Changed public API, schema, IPC channel or config: are all consumers updated?
Listeners/timers/intervals never cleaned up, unbounded growth, closures capturing large objects.
O(n^2) searches, queries or awaits inside loops, repeated work on hot paths.
New or unpinned dependencies, known-vulnerable packages.
New behaviour without a test, or missing edge cases for the change.
Does the PR body show before/after evidence (failing test now passing, screenshot), not just 'tests green'?
Long functions, mixed responsibilities, duplicated logic in the changed hunks (possible smell).
Names that do not reveal intent (possible smell).
